draft.title: The outbreak of war in 1939
card: In August 1939, Germany and the Soviet Union signed the Nazi-Soviet Pact, also called the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact. Each promised not to attack the other.
A secret part of the pact divided Eastern Europe into German and Soviet zones of influence, including Poland. Hitler no longer had to fear a war on two fronts if he attacked Poland.
Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. Britain and France had promised to support Poland, and they declared war on Germany on 3 September.
The Soviet Union invaded eastern Poland on 17 September 1939. Poland was then divided between Germany and the Soviet Union.
draft.remember: The pact removed Hitler's fear of a two-front war, so he invaded Poland, and Britain and France then declared war.

a.q: Why did the Nazi-Soviet Pact make it easier for Germany to invade Poland?
opts: It removed the risk of a war against the Soviet Union too
It gave Germany control of Soviet armies and weapons
It forced Britain and France to promise not to fight
It made Poland agree to give up its eastern land
a.why: Each side promised not to attack the other, so Hitler did not have to fight on two fronts. The pact did not stop Britain and France, who had promised to support Poland and declared war after the invasion.
a.clue: Think about which other country Hitler would have had to fight.

b.q: A student says the pact caused Britain and France to declare war in 1939. Which reply is most accurate?
opts: It cleared the way for the invasion that led to their declaration
It was an alliance that Britain and France had to answer
It was an attack on Britain and France, so they declared war
It had no link to the invasion of Poland or the declarations
b.why: The pact cleared the way for Germany to invade Poland, and the invasion led Britain and France to declare war because of their promise to Poland. The pact itself was between Germany and the Soviet Union, so it was not a direct act against Britain and France.
b.clue: Follow the chain from the pact, to the invasion, to the declaration.
